question: How many digits are in the base-ten representation of \(8^5 \cdot 5^{10} \cdot 15^5?\)
solution:
All three exponents are multiples of \(5\), so the expression can be combined into one fifth power.

Using \(5^{10}=(5^2)^5\) and the rule that a product of fifth powers is the fifth power of the product, we obtain
\[
8^5\cdot5^{10}\cdot15^5
=(8\cdot5^2\cdot15)^5
=3000^5.
\]
Since \(3000=3\cdot10^3\), this becomes
\[
3000^5=3^5\cdot10^{15}=243\cdot10^{15}.
\]
Multiplying \(243\) by \(10^{15}\) appends \(15\) zeros to its three digits. The number therefore has \(3+15=\boxed{18}\) digits, choice E.
